title: Sixth Word Applying The Comparison Selling The Trust

questions.question: In the parable’s explanation, who does the king represent?
questions.answer: He represents Allah, the eternal Lord, Sustainer, and Creator.

questions.question: What do the estate and equipment in the parable stand for in a human life?
questions.answer: They stand for the things a person has in this life, including the body, soul, heart, and human faculties.

questions.question: Which human abilities are mentioned as part of this trust?
questions.answer: Outer and inner senses such as sight and speech, along with intellect and imagination.

questions.question: Who is represented by the noble lieutenant?
questions.answer: The Messenger of Allah.

questions.question: What does the decree in the parable refer to?
questions.answer: It refers to the Qur’an.

questions.question: What idea is the battlefield meant to bring to a person’s mind?
questions.answer: That this world is always changing and passing away, so people wonder how anything can be preserved permanently.

questions.question: What answer does the Qur’an give to the fear of losing everything?
questions.answer: It says there is a good and easy way to turn what passes away into something lasting.

questions.question: What is that way?
questions.answer: To return the trust to its real Owner by giving oneself and one’s possessions to Allah.

questions.question: What central lesson is drawn from the parable for the human self?
questions.answer: A person should recognize that everything he has is a trust from Allah and should be devoted back to Him.

questions.question: In the explanation of the parable, what do a person’s body, spirit, heart, and senses all have in common?
questions.answer: They are all part of the trust given during worldly life.

questions.question: Why is the world compared to a battlefield with constant upheaval?
questions.answer: Because it is unstable, always changing, and nothing in it remains in a person’s possession forever.

questions.question: What question naturally arises when a person sees the world’s instability?
questions.answer: He wonders whether there is a way to keep what would otherwise be lost.

questions.question: How does the Qur’anic message respond to that question?
questions.answer: It offers a beautiful and simple path to preserve what would otherwise vanish.

questions.question: What does “selling the trust” mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means giving one’s life and possessions over to Allah by using them as He wants.

questions.question: Why is this “sale” actually a gain rather than a loss?
questions.answer: Because what is temporary is turned into something lasting and richly rewarded.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the future of a life spent for Allah?
questions.answer: Its moments may seem to pass, but they become lasting blessings with eternal results.

questions.question: What reward is named as the price for this transaction?
questions.answer: Paradise.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does the parable help the self see more clearly?
questions.answer: It helps the self recognize the real meaning of life, possessions, and their relationship to Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage identify as the true owner of the trust humans hold?
questions.answer: Allah alone.

questions.question: Which two sacred guides are linked to the explanation of the parable?
questions.answer: The Messenger of Allah and the Qur’an.

questions.question: Why does the world’s constant change push a person to think deeply?
questions.answer: Because it shows that worldly things slip away and cannot be kept by human power.

questions.question: What solution is presented for preserving what seems certain to disappear?
questions.answer: Returning it to Allah through obedience and sincere devotion.

questions.question: What transformation happens to temporary life when it is spent for Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes a source of everlasting benefit.

questions.question: Besides becoming everlasting, what direct reward is promised in this trade?
questions.answer: Entry into Paradise.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the parable and the “truth” the self is asked to see?
questions.answer: The parable is a teaching tool that explains the real meaning of human life and responsibility before Allah.

questions.question: In the passage, what belongs to the category of “your possessions” in life?
questions.answer: Everything entrusted to a person, including physical life and inward faculties.

questions.question: Why is the Prophet represented as a noble lieutenant in the explanation?
questions.answer: Because he conveys the command and guidance of the true King.

questions.question: What role does the Qur’an play in the explanation of the parable?
questions.answer: It gives the divine message that explains the profitable transaction.

questions.question: Why does the world make people ask whether anything can be kept?
questions.answer: Because everything in it is unstable and keeps slipping away.

questions.question: What does the passage identify as the way to preserve what is passing?
questions.answer: Handing the trust back to Allah by living in obedience to Him.

questions.question: How many benefits are promised from this exchange?
questions.answer: Five.

questions.question: What does the first benefit teach about time and mortality?
questions.answer: That a passing life does not become meaningless if it is spent for Allah, because it gains eternal fruit.

questions.question: What does the second benefit reveal about Allah’s generosity?
questions.answer: That He grants Paradise in return for what was already His trust.

questions.question: What does the passage want the self to understand through the parable’s symbols?
questions.answer: That human life and abilities are entrusted by Allah and should be returned to Him through faithful use.

questions.question: What are some examples of the “inner and outer” faculties included in that trust?
questions.answer: The eye, tongue, intellect, imagination, heart, and spirit.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the condition of the world?
questions.answer: As unstable, constantly shifting, and never secure.

questions.question: Why does that unstable condition matter spiritually?
questions.answer: It pushes a person to seek a way to make his life and deeds endure beyond worldly loss.

questions.question: What is the “trade” offered in the passage?
questions.answer: Giving oneself and one’s possessions to Allah by using them for His sake.

questions.question: What is the first profit in terms of life’s meaning?
questions.answer: A short worldly life gains permanent value.

questions.question: What is the second profit in terms of reward?
questions.answer: A person is promised Paradise.

questions.question: In the explained parable, what does the king’s identity teach about ownership?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah is the true owner of everything a person has.

questions.question: What is included in the trust besides wealth or outward possessions?
questions.answer: A person’s body, soul, heart, senses, intellect, and imagination.

questions.question: Why is the Messenger of Allah linked with the noble lieutenant?
questions.answer: Because he delivers the divine message that explains how to handle the trust.

questions.question: What does the Qur’an do in this passage?
questions.answer: It announces the offer of exchange and explains its benefits.

questions.question: What truth is pictured by the battlefield image?
questions.answer: The world is unstable and everything in it is exposed to change and loss.

questions.question: What human concern arises from that instability?
questions.answer: People want to know whether what they lose can be preserved in another way.

questions.question: What answer does revelation give to that concern?
questions.answer: What is entrusted to us can be preserved by returning it to Allah through sincere obedience.

questions.question: What is the basic meaning of “selling” oneself and one’s property to Allah here?
questions.answer: It means dedicating all one has and is to Allah’s service.

questions.question: What is the first of the five gains?
questions.answer: Temporary life becomes lasting in its outcome.

questions.question: What is the second?
questions.answer: Paradise is granted.
